objects.description: Describes a libffi data type used to define function argument and return types. Fields hold the ABI-computed size, alignment, a type code (FFI_TYPE_*), and for structs the NULL-terminated array of element type pointers. Instances for builtin types are provided as extern variables (e.g., ffi_type_uint32).
Status code enum returned by many libffi APIs; indicates success or various errors related to type definitions, ABI, or argument types.
Call interface descriptor. Describes the ABI, number of arguments, argument type array, return type, and computed call frame info for invoking a function through libffi.

Packed argument word used by the raw calling interface. Represents one machine word of argument data in multiple views. ffi_java_raw is an alias or a narrower variant for Java-style packing on some ABIs.
Executable closure object encapsulating a callable trampoline plus a user callback. When prepared, code in tramp invokes fun with the associated ffi_cif and user_data.
Closure variant for the raw API. Calls user-provided fun with arguments presented as an array of ffi_raw words. May include an internal translator on platforms without native raw support.
Closure variant for the Java raw API, passing arguments as ffi_java_raw words according to Java-style packing. Some related APIs are deprecated.
Closure structure for Go interop. Holds a trampoline pointer, an ffi_cif, and a callback function to be invoked from the trampoline.

objects.definition:
typedef enum ffi_abi {
#if defined(X86_WIN64)
  FFI_FIRST_ABI = 0,
  FFI_WIN64,
  FFI_GNUW64,
  FFI_LAST_ABI,
#ifdef __GNUC__
  FFI_DEFAULT_ABI = FFI_GNUW64
#else
  FFI_DEFAULT_ABI = FFI_WIN64
#endif

#elif defined(X86_64) || (defined (__x86_64__) && defined (X86_DARWIN))
  FFI_FIRST_ABI = 1,
  FFI_UNIX64,
  FFI_WIN64,
  FFI_EFI64 = FFI_WIN64,
  FFI_GNUW64,
  FFI_LAST_ABI,
  FFI_DEFAULT_ABI = FFI_UNIX64

#elif defined(X86_WIN32)
  FFI_FIRST_ABI = 0,
  FFI_SYSV      = 1,
  FFI_STDCALL   = 2,
  FFI_THISCALL  = 3,
  FFI_FASTCALL  = 4,
  FFI_MS_CDECL  = 5,
  FFI_PASCAL    = 6,
  FFI_REGISTER  = 7,
  FFI_LAST_ABI,
  FFI_DEFAULT_ABI = FFI_MS_CDECL
#else
  FFI_FIRST_ABI = 0,
  FFI_SYSV      = 1,
  FFI_THISCALL  = 3,
  FFI_FASTCALL  = 4,
  FFI_STDCALL   = 5,
  FFI_PASCAL    = 6,
  FFI_REGISTER  = 7,
  FFI_MS_CDECL  = 8,
  FFI_LAST_ABI,
  FFI_DEFAULT_ABI = FFI_SYSV
#endif
} ffi_abi;
objects.description: Enumeration of supported ABIs for the current target. Determines calling convention and argument passing rules used when preparing a call interface (ffi_cif). Values vary by platform macros.

functions.name: ffi_raw_call
functions.description: Invokes a function pointer using libffi’s raw calling convention. The arguments are passed via an array of ffi_raw entries instead of a void**. Use when you’ve prepared a CIF and packed arguments into ffi_raw. rvalue points to storage for the return value (or may be unused for void returns).
requirements: cif must be initialized by a successful call to ffi_prep_cif or ffi_prep_cif_var for the target function and ABI.
fn must be a valid callable function pointer compatible with the CIF’s ABI and prototype.
avalue must reference at least cif->nargs entries packed according to the raw ABI for each argument type described by cif->arg_types.
rvalue must point to writable storage large enough for the CIF’s return type; if the return type is void, rvalue may be ignored/unused.
The effective argument and return types must match those in cif to avoid undefined behavior.

functions.name: ffi_ptrarray_to_raw
functions.description: Converts an array of pointers to argument values (void**) into the raw ffi_raw array format for use with ffi_raw_call.
requirements: cif must be prepared (ffi_prep_cif/ffi_prep_cif_var).
args must have at least cif->nargs elements, each pointing to a value of the corresponding type in cif->arg_types.
raw must point to storage for at least cif->nargs ffi_raw entries.
Argument values must be initialized and match the types specified by cif.

functions.name: ffi_raw_to_ptrarray
functions.description: Converts an array of raw arguments (ffi_raw) into an array of pointers (void**) to typed argument storage.
requirements: cif must be prepared (ffi_prep_cif/ffi_prep_cif_var).
raw must reference at least cif->nargs elements encoded per cif->arg_types.

args must have space for at least cif->nargs entries and be populated with pointers to appropriately typed storage provided by the caller, or receive pointers as produced by this conversion depending on platform conventions. Details of pointed-to storage ownership are not specified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: ffi_raw_size
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes required to hold the raw argument array for the given CIF when using the raw calling convention.
requirements: cif must be prepared (ffi_prep_cif/ffi_prep_cif_var).

functions.name: ffi_java_raw_call
functions.description: Invokes a function using the Java-style raw calling convention, where 64-bit longs/doubles may consume additional slots on some ABIs. Deprecated API retained for compatibility.
requirements: cif must be prepared (ffi_prep_cif/ffi_prep_cif_var).
fn must be a valid callable function pointer compatible with the CIF’s ABI and prototype.
avalue must contain at least cif->nargs entries packed per the Java raw convention.
rvalue must point to writable storage suitable for the return type; ignored for void returns.
Callers should prefer non-Java raw or standard APIs due to deprecation.

functions.name: ffi_java_ptrarray_to_raw
functions.description: Converts a pointer array of arguments to the Java raw argument array representation. Deprecated.
requirements: cif must be prepared.
args must have at least cif->nargs elements pointing to properly typed values.
raw must have space for at least cif->nargs entries encoded per the Java raw convention.
Deprecated; prefer non-Java raw or standard APIs.

functions.name: ffi_java_raw_to_ptrarray
functions.description: Converts Java raw arguments into a pointer array form. Deprecated.
requirements: cif must be prepared.
raw must contain at least cif->nargs entries encoded per the Java raw convention.
args must have capacity for at least cif->nargs pointers.
Deprecated; prefer non-Java raw or standard APIs.

functions.name: ffi_java_raw_size
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes required to hold the Java raw argument array for the given CIF. Deprecated.
requirements: cif must be prepared.
Deprecated API; usage should be avoided in new code.

functions.name: ffi_get_version
functions.description: Returns the libffi version string (e.g., "3.5.2"). Useful for logging or runtime feature checks.

functions.name: ffi_get_version_number
functions.description: Returns the libffi version as a numeric value encoded as (major*10000 + minor*100 + patch).

functions.name: ffi_get_default_abi
functions.description: Returns the default ABI identifier for the current target (one of ffi_abi values).

functions.name: ffi_get_closure_size
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of an ffi closure/trampoline allocation unit on this platform. Useful for sizing buffers or allocations for closures.

functions.name: ffi_closure_alloc
functions.description: Allocates executable memory suitable for creating a closure trampoline. Returns a writable memory address; stores the executable entry-point address in *code for invocation.
requirements: code must be a valid pointer to receive the entry-point address (code != NULL).
size must be sufficient for the closure/trampoline being created; typical use is sizeof(ffi_closure) or ffi_get_closure_size(), but exact minimum is not specified here (unknown).
The returned memory must be released with ffi_closure_free.

functions.name: ffi_closure_free
functions.description: Frees memory previously allocated by ffi_closure_alloc, releasing any associated executable mapping.
requirements: The argument must be a pointer previously returned by ffi_closure_alloc, or NULL if allowed by implementation (NULL behavior not specified in this header; unknown).
Must not be used to free memory not allocated by ffi_closure_alloc.

functions.name: ffi_prep_closure
functions.signature: ffi_status ffi_prep_closure(ffi_closure *closure, ffi_cif *cif, void (*fun)(ffi_cif*, void*, void**, void*), void *user_data);
functions.description: Initializes a closure to invoke the callback 'fun' when the closure’s entry point is called. Associates the given CIF and user_data. Deprecated in favor of ffi_prep_closure_loc.
requirements: closure must point to writable memory suitable for an ffi_closure (often from ffi_closure_alloc).
cif must be prepared (ffi_prep_cif/ffi_prep_cif_var) describing the callback’s call interface.
fun must be a valid function pointer matching the expected closure callback signature.
Deprecated; prefer ffi_prep_closure_loc.

functions.name: ffi_prep_closure_loc
functions.signature: ffi_status ffi_prep_closure_loc(ffi_closure *closure, ffi_cif *cif, void (*fun)(ffi_cif*, void*, void**, void*), void *user_data, void *codeloc);
functions.description: Initializes a closure and binds it to a specific executable entry-point address (codeloc). Use the address stored from ffi_closure_alloc via its code out-parameter.
requirements: closure must point to writable memory suitable for an ffi_closure (often from ffi_closure_alloc).
cif must be prepared for the callback signature.
fun must be a valid function pointer matching the closure callback signature.
codeloc must be the executable entry-point address associated with the closure memory (typically the value written to *code by ffi_closure_alloc).

functions.name: ffi_prep_raw_closure
functions.signature: ffi_status ffi_prep_raw_closure(ffi_raw_closure *closure, ffi_cif *cif, void (*fun)(ffi_cif*, void*, ffi_raw*, void*), void *user_data);
functions.description: Initializes a raw closure that passes arguments to the callback as an ffi_raw array rather than void**.
requirements: closure must point to writable memory suitable for an ffi_raw_closure.
cif must be prepared for the function signature.
fun must be a valid function pointer taking ffi_raw* arguments.
The closure memory should be allocated appropriately (e.g., via ffi_closure_alloc) before preparation.

functions.name: ffi_prep_raw_closure_loc
functions.signature: ffi_status ffi_prep_raw_closure_loc(ffi_raw_closure *closure, ffi_cif *cif, void (*fun)(ffi_cif*, void*, ffi_raw*, void*), void *user_data, void *codeloc);
functions.description: Initializes a raw closure and associates it with a specific executable entry-point address (codeloc).
requirements: closure must point to writable memory for an ffi_raw_closure.
cif must be prepared.
fun must be a valid function pointer taking ffi_raw* arguments.
codeloc must be the executable entry-point where the closure trampoline resides (typically from ffi_closure_alloc).

functions.name: ffi_prep_java_raw_closure
functions.signature: ffi_status ffi_prep_java_raw_closure(ffi_java_raw_closure *closure, ffi_cif *cif, void (*fun)(ffi_cif*, void*, ffi_java_raw*, void*), void *user_data);
functions.description: Initializes a Java-style raw closure that delivers arguments as ffi_java_raw to the callback. Deprecated.
requirements: closure must point to writable memory for an ffi_java_raw_closure.
cif must be prepared.
fun must be a valid function pointer taking ffi_java_raw* arguments.
Deprecated; prefer non-Java raw or standard closures.

functions.name: ffi_prep_java_raw_closure_loc
functions.signature: ffi_status ffi_prep_java_raw_closure_loc(ffi_java_raw_closure *closure, ffi_cif *cif, void (*fun)(ffi_cif*, void*, ffi_java_raw*, void*), void *user_data, void *codeloc);
functions.description: Initializes a Java-style raw closure and binds it to the specified executable entry-point address. Deprecated.
requirements: closure must point to writable memory for an ffi_java_raw_closure.
cif must be prepared.
fun must be a valid function pointer taking ffi_java_raw* arguments.
codeloc must be the executable entry-point associated with the closure allocation.
Deprecated API.

functions.name: ffi_prep_go_closure
functions.signature: ffi_status ffi_prep_go_closure(ffi_go_closure *closure, ffi_cif *cif, void (*fun)(ffi_cif*, void*, void**, void*));
functions.description: Initializes a Go-style closure record so that calls can be bridged into a callback fun using the provided CIF. Intended for libffi’s Go interop support.
requirements: closure must point to writable memory for an ffi_go_closure.
cif must be prepared for the callback signature.
fun must be a valid function pointer matching the callback signature.

functions.name: ffi_call_go
functions.signature: void ffi_call_go(ffi_cif *cif, void (*fn)(void), void *rvalue, void **avalue, void *closure);
functions.description: Invokes a function pointer like ffi_call but with additional closure/context pointer for Go interop. The closure parameter supplies context needed by the Go bridge.
requirements: cif must be prepared (ffi_prep_cif/ffi_prep_cif_var).
fn must be a valid callable function pointer compatible with cif.
avalue must point to an array of at least cif->nargs pointers to argument values matching cif->arg_types.
rvalue must point to writable storage adequate for the return type (or may be unused for void returns).
closure must be a valid context pointer expected by the Go bridge (semantics not specified here; unknown).

functions.name: ffi_prep_cif
functions.signature: ffi_status ffi_prep_cif(ffi_cif *cif, ffi_abi abi, unsigned int nargs, ffi_type *rtype, ffi_type **atypes);
functions.description: Initializes a call interface (cif) describing a non-variadic function: ABI, number of arguments, their types, and return type. Must be called before ffi_call or closure preparation.
requirements: cif must point to writable memory for an ffi_cif.
abi must be a valid ffi_abi for the current target (e.g., ffi_get_default_abi or a specific constant).
atypes must point to an array of at least nargs pointers to ffi_type descriptors describing each argument.
rtype must point to a valid ffi_type describing the return type.
nargs must match the number of provided argument type pointers in atypes.

functions.name: ffi_prep_cif_var
functions.signature: ffi_status ffi_prep_cif_var(ffi_cif *cif, ffi_abi abi, unsigned int nfixedargs, unsigned int ntotalargs, ffi_type *rtype, ffi_type **atypes);
functions.description: Initializes a call interface for a variadic function, specifying the count of fixed arguments and the total number of arguments for a particular call context.
requirements: cif must point to writable memory for an ffi_cif.
abi must be a valid ffi_abi for the current target.
nfixedargs specifies the number of leading fixed parameters; must be <= ntotalargs.
ntotalargs is the total number of arguments that will be passed in the call.
atypes must reference an array of at least ntotalargs entries describing all arguments for the call.
rtype must point to a valid ffi_type describing the return type.

functions.name: ffi_call
functions.description: Invokes a function pointer according to the call interface specified by cif, passing arguments from avalue and storing the return value in rvalue.
requirements: cif must be prepared by ffi_prep_cif or ffi_prep_cif_var for the target function.
fn must be a valid callable function pointer compatible with the CIF’s ABI and types.
avalue must point to an array with at least cif->nargs entries, each a pointer to a value matching the corresponding ffi_type in cif->arg_types.
rvalue must point to writable storage large enough for the return type; if return type is void, rvalue may be ignored/unused.

functions.name: ffi_get_struct_offsets
functions.description: Computes and returns the byte offsets of each field within a struct described by struct_type for the specified ABI, writing them into the offsets array.
requirements: abi must be a valid ffi_abi supported on this platform.
struct_type must describe an ffi_type with type == FFI_TYPE_STRUCT (i.e., a structure with elements).
offsets must point to an array with at least as many entries as fields in struct_type->elements; exact count should match the number of elements (terminated by NULL in typical libffi usage).

unharnessable_functions.name: ffi_raw_call
unharnessable_functions.reason: Requires invoking an arbitrary function pointer with a prepared CIF; providing a valid, safe callback function is not possible without defining new code.

unharnessable_functions.name: ffi_java_raw_call
unharnessable_functions.reason: Requires a valid callable function pointer compatible with the CIF; a safe callback cannot be provided under the no-new-functions constraint.

unharnessable_functions.name: ffi_prep_closure
unharnessable_functions.reason: Needs a valid callback function pointer matching the closure signature, which cannot be safely provided without defining new code.

unharnessable_functions.name: ffi_prep_closure_loc
unharnessable_functions.reason: Requires a valid callback function pointer and executable trampoline target; providing such a function is not possible without defining new code.

unharnessable_functions.name: ffi_prep_raw_closure
unharnessable_functions.reason: Requires a user callback of type void(ffi_cif*,void*,ffi_raw*,void*); cannot be supplied under the no-new-functions constraint.

unharnessable_functions.name: ffi_prep_raw_closure_loc
unharnessable_functions.reason: Requires a valid user callback and codeloc; a safe callback cannot be provided without defining new code.

unharnessable_functions.name: ffi_prep_java_raw_closure
unharnessable_functions.reason: Needs a valid user callback function pointer; defining such a function is disallowed in this harness model.

unharnessable_functions.name: ffi_prep_java_raw_closure_loc
unharnessable_functions.reason: Requires a valid user callback and trampoline codeloc; providing a safe callback is not possible without defining new code.

unharnessable_functions.name: ffi_prep_go_closure
unharnessable_functions.reason: Requires providing a C callback function pointer, which cannot be safely defined within the stub under the no new top-level functions constraint.

unharnessable_functions.name: ffi_call_go
unharnessable_functions.reason: Requires invoking an arbitrary function pointer; supplying a valid callable target with matching prototype is not possible under the stub constraints.

unharnessable_functions.name: ffi_call
unharnessable_functions.reason: Requires a valid function pointer target with a matching prototype, which cannot be safely provided without defining external functions or closures.
